format: Cases without op: merge(server, local, base) = expect. server, local and base hold only the envelope parts the merge reads (fields, stamps; base null for a create); any other top-level key is an unknown key that must survive from the server, and the local side's are not carried. expect is the merged envelope; needsTextMerge lists the T fields that need the three-way text merge (absent when none). expectLosses lists, in field order, the S fields and S elements (element names the key) where a local value different from the server's lost because the server had moved them since the base, with the type's onServerFirstLoss hook when it declares one (type names the record type for that lookup); absent means none. The policy letter is the server stamp's first character (a T stamp on a map element merges like S, with no text merge). mintedAgainst, when present, lists ({field, element?, stamp}) the local paths whose stamps this device minted and pinned, each with the stamp it was minted against (the version of that field or element the writer saw, §6.3); a path it does not list has no provenance, and an entry naming a map or set field without an element gives none of its elements provenance. For each field the local side stamped: skip it when its stamp equals the base's or the server's (the local side then holds the server's own write); take the local value and stamp when the server has none; a scalar stamp on one side and per-key stamps on the other keep the server's field. L: when exactly one side's value is one of the field's terminalValues in the schema of type (Card.status retired), that side's value and stamp win whatever the stamps; otherwise the local value wins when the local stamp is later, or when the path's mintedAgainst stamp equals both the server's stamp and the base's (the writer edited exactly the version the server still holds). Every path without that provenance goes by stamp order: a stub edit forwarded verbatim, pending fields re-applied to a moved copy, a reconciling Mac's pending changes, late-import patches. S and T: the local value wins only when the server's stamp equals the base's; otherwise S keeps the server's (a loss when the values differ) and T keeps the server's and lists the field in needsTextMerge. X and N: the larger or smaller value, the server's on a tie or when the two do not compare, under the later of the two stamps. Stamps order by the 27 characters after the letter, as plain strings, never clamped (§6.3 as corrected by WP2: a clamp with its tie broken by those characters is the same order). Map and set fields carry one stamp per key and merge per key by the same rules. X and N compare numbers, arrays of numbers lexicographically (a prefix first), and objects by their ord array (the winning object is taken whole); anything else does not compare. Cases with op compact: the next writer of record drops every removal marker whose stamp's milliseconds are more than compactionHorizonDays before now; type names the record type whose schema says which fields are maps (marker: a null value) and sets (marker: false); scalars, fields the schema does not list and types it does not know are never compacted. Cases with op splitKeptCard: the Card.kept hook for the card cardID given the server's card and the lost Keep = expect, the new card ({type, id, fields}) or null: null when the lost Keep has no fingerprint, has the server Keep's fingerprint or equals it; else id card:<deckSourceID>:<seedKey> with seedKey split:<cardID>:<the first 16 hex characters of sha256 of the lost fingerprint>, fields status kept, deckSourceID, seedKey, kept (the lost Keep), splitFrom (cardID), keptAt (the lost Keep's at, when present) and the server's origin, madeBy, draftedAt and legacy when present.
status: WP1's seed cases first (each re-checked against the reference), then WP2's: every policy against every situation, X and N value domains, maps, sets, far-future stamps and provenance (mintedAgainst) for every path that copies or re-applies stamps, terminal values, unknown fields, lost first writes with their hooks, idempotence, type-aware compaction, the splitKeptCard output, and 70 seeded random cases. Built by scripts/schema/build-vectors.mjs, whose reference merge is independent of both sync cores; regenerate with it, never by hand.
